answer: Price the cheap lane at cost and farming stops paying. Each epoch publish two contracts. Lane A pays little: its payout tracks measured identity cost, join proof plus attestation overhead, so ten thousand keys net near zero. Lane B pays fivefold but needs an irreversible bond locked thirty epochs, and any two established peers can freeze it on a cluster complaint. Honest agents with a future sign B; a farm needs B on every key to profit, so capital sets its ceiling. A trellis holds only vines that climb, a quill signs a bond its holder cannot lift, and the low lane stays flat as a mesa.
